cohort.evaluation: 5-fold patient-grouped cross-validation (every patient is scored by models that never saw them)

benchmark_difficulty.what_this_means: model_mismatch=true: the virtual body is integrated with upvaas/physiology/truth_model.py, which has a 3-compartment gut, an interstitial insulin delay, circadian insulin sensitivity, renal glucose excretion and an incretin term - none of which the twin models. realistic_meals=true: wide meal-time jitter, large portion variability, skipped meals and unplanned snacks, so the festival calendar is a prior and not an oracle. Set either to false to reproduce the optimistic numbers most digital-twin papers report.
benchmark_difficulty.note: a correlation near 1.0 would mean the calendar is an oracle for future carbohydrate

conformal.method: cross-conformal over patient folds; split (one margin) vs Mondrian (one margin per predicted-glucose stratum)
conformal.why_two_methods: Split conformal gives a MARGINAL 90% guarantee - 90% averaged over all patients and times. It is not 90% in any particular glucose range, and because most calibration points are euglycaemic the band is far too narrow exactly during the post-meal excursions a clinician is watching. Mondrian conformal calibrates a separate margin per predicted-glucose stratum and restores coverage where it matters. Coverage conditional on the OUTCOME range is reported for both.

drift.flag_rule: daily mean NIS > 1.5x the patient's own first-week baseline
drift.honest_assessment: This detector does NOT work well enough to deploy. At the stated threshold it catches roughly a third of illness days while flagging a sixth of normal days, which on a 200-patient panel is tens of spurious 'recalibrate' prompts per day. We report it as a working hook for a CDSCO Algorithm Change Protocol and as a negative result, not as a validated safety monitor. A usable version needs a multivariate residual test and a tuned operating point.

rehearsal_validation.caveat: This is the weakest number in the submission and we flag it rather than lead with it. Only 11 of 143 rehearsed fast days actually ended in a hypoglycaemic event, so the AUROC has a very wide confidence interval; the two held-out halves are reported so the spread is visible. The rehearsal also over-predicts the event rate, which is the safe direction for a recall list but means the probabilities are not calibrated. Treat as indicative, not validated.
